**That change gives the NDJSON a longer life than the checkpoint, which is a lifetime question the old code never had to answer.** `stop()` used to delete the file because the array had replaced it; it now drops only the UserDefaults checkpoint, so a finished run stops offering "Recover unsaved run?" while keeping the payload it is about to upload. `reset()` deletes it, and `start()` sweeps any other track file in the directory — which also closes a pre-existing leak, since discarding a recovery cleared the checkpoint and stranded its NDJSON forever.

**Verification.** Wear OS is compiled and green locally (`./gradlew assembleDebug testDebugUnitTest`, 573 tests). **The Swift is uncompiled** — this repo's toolchain is Linux-only, so the macOS CI job (`xcodebuild test`, `test-watch-ios`) is the first compile and the first run of the new XCTest cases, as it was for § 436. The memory figures above are derived from the struct layouts and the 1 Hz target, not measured on a device; an Instruments allocations trace over a long recording is a bench item, and `parity.md`'s ultra row stays `Partial` on Apple Watch for exactly that reason.

## 468. The antimeridian fix crosses back from the watch to web and mobile, and the normalisation is owned once per platform

**Date:** 2026-08-03

[§ 463](#463-the-along-course-axis-inherits-the-courses-topology-and-the-forward-bias-may-never-outrank-the-geometry) fixed the antimeridian in `watch_core` and deliberately left the web/mobile originals alone, because `route_geometry` and `route_snap` on the wrist are one-way ports tested case-for-case against the web suite and fixing the copy would have broken the port without fixing the product. Issue #664 carried the debt forward; this closes it web-first, then mirrors.

**The defect is the same one line, and web has it in five places, not the four the issue named.** `route_geometry.distanceAlongRoute`'s per-segment frame and `interpolateAlongRoute`'s longitude lerp; `route_snap.snapToPolyline`'s frame and its snapped longitude; `route_simplify`'s RDP perpendicular distance (which converts each longitude to metres east of the prime meridian and *then* subtracts — the same subtraction wearing a different shape) and `summarizeRouteFromTrack`'s equirectangular leg; `track_projection.projectTrack`'s bounding box; and `run_heatmap.heatBounds`'s fit box. **`privacy` was named in the issue and needed no change at all** — its only geometry is haversine, and `sin`/`cos` are periodic, so a whole-turn error cancels. That absence is now pinned by a test on both platforms rather than argued for in a commit message, because "we looked and there was nothing" is indistinguishable from "we forgot" a year later.

**The two bounding-box sites are the same defect with a louder symptom.** A raw min/max over longitudes reads a track straddling 180° as spanning 359.99°, so the thumbnail's fitted scale collapses and the route renders as a dot, and the heatmap fits the whole planet instead of the runner's streets — exactly what § 463 saw on the wrist's Nav panel. Their fix is not a delta but an *unwrap*: every longitude is expressed on the first point's side of the line, and the resulting east edge is allowed to sit past 180. Both MapLibre and flutter_map read that as the adjacent world copy, which is the intent; clamping it back into range would reintroduce the wrap the box exists to avoid.

**`unwrapLonDeg` is deliberately not the watch's formula.** `watch_core::geo` writes it `reference + lon_delta_deg(reference, lon)`, which is correct but rounds: a subtraction followed by an addition need not return the input bit for bit. Web and mobile write it as the longitude less whole turns, so the `floor` is exactly zero within a hemisphere and the value comes back untouched. That matters more here than on the wrist, because these five sites feed pinned test values on two platforms and the bar for this change was that **not one existing expected number moves** — 20 route_simplify, 38 route_geometry, 10 route_snap, 4 track_projection, 13 run_heatmap, 8 privacy on web, and their Dart mirrors, all unchanged. `lonDeltaDeg` and `wrapLonDeg` are the watch's semantics exactly, opposite meridians and non-finite propagation included.

**The helper is a new parity pair** (`apps/web/src/lib/routes/geo.ts` ↔ `apps/mobile_android/lib/geo.dart`), sited in `routes/` because every consumer today lives there. Four planar sites outside the issue's scope still carry the raw subtraction and are **not** fixed here: `routing_quality.ts`'s projection frame, `nearest_track_point.ts`'s bbox grid, `route_loop.ts`'s synthetic-curve delta, and `RunTrackPreview.svelte`'s 5 m "is this track worth drawing" span. None is a lockstep pair, each is a separate behaviour change with its own test surface, and folding them in would have made this diff impossible to review against the identity bar above. They are the follow-up.

**Verification: unit-tested on both platforms.** 3,130 web tests pass (2 skipped, none new); the Dart side is green across every suite that touches the six modules (413 tests). Thirty-three new cases — 17 web, 16 Dart, the odd one being the web-only `summarizeRouteFromTrack` — of which twelve carry the helper's own contract (the watch's six tests, mirrored) and the rest pin a behaviour that used to be wrong: a leg interpolated across the line, a fix projected onto one, a marker snapped past it, a straight line collapsing under RDP where it previously kept every interior point, a real deviation still surviving, a thumbnail box matching the identical box a degree west, and a heatmap box spanning the runner's own streets. Nothing here is verified against a real GPS trace near 180° — no fixture in the repo carries one — so this is host-tested only, the same rung the watch's half of the fix claims.

## 469. The per-cue voice map becomes `UD`, because the surface that edits a preference is not the surface that obeys it

**Date:** 2026-08-03

**Amends [§ 295](#295-voice-cues-become-a-per-cue-registry-race-guidance-speaks-corrections-not-verdicts-10-10-10-is-a-phase-plan-preset-marker-targets-live-in-marker-meta) (issue #607).** § 295 made `voice_cue_types` device-scoped, reasoning from playback: recording is mobile-only (§ 235), so the phone that speaks the cue is the phone that should own the toggle. That holds for *obeying* the preference and fails for *editing* it. Web is the canonical feature surface (§ 24), the settings UI was owed there, and a browser mints its own `device_id` — so a web write to `user_device_settings` lands on a row belonging to a device that will never record, and the phone would never read it. A device-scoped key is unreachable from the one client that is supposed to own settings.

**So the key is `UD`, and the two clients write different bags on purpose.** The mobile cue switches keep writing the device bag (a runner with a race phone and a training phone can still differ); `/settings/preferences` writes the universal bag like every other control on that page. `SettingsSyncService` applies universal first and device second, and `applyVoiceCueTypes` merges entry-by-entry rather than replacing, so the overlay is per-cue: a device value wins for the ids it names, a universal value lands for the ids it doesn't, and an id in neither stays audible. That last property is § 295's absent-id-is-on rule surviving the promotion — it is why the merge could not become an assignment.

**The web write merges too, for a different reason.** `updateUniversal` replaces a top-level key, so the page must send the whole map. It sends the loaded map with one entry changed, so a cue id this build has never heard of keeps whatever the runner chose for it on a newer client. Symmetrically, `readVoiceCueMap` drops any non-boolean entry instead of coercing it: a malformed bag can only ever lose a suppression, never invent one, which keeps a corrupt value from silencing a cue nobody turned off.

**The cue ids are now a wire contract with two owners, so a test enforces it.** They were previously only Dart constants. `voice_cues.test.ts` reads `apps/mobile_android/lib/preferences.dart` and asserts the id list and its order match `VOICE_CUE_IDS` exactly — a web toggle writing a key the recorder doesn't read is silent, not loud, and silence is the failure this surface exists to prevent. The label mapping is keyed `Record<VoiceCueId, …>` so a cue with no i18n row is a compile error rather than a blank line. Writing that guard surfaced that `apps/web`'s CI glob was `src/lib/**/*.test.ts`, so the one existing source guard under `src/routes` had never run; it is now `src/**/*.test.ts`.

**Not fixed here, and worth naming:** `voice_feedback_enabled` (the master toggle) has the same shape and is still broken in the same way — registered `D`, written by web to the universal bag, and read by mobile only from the device bag, so the web toggle has never reached a phone. `parity.md` asserted the opposite. The fix is the same four lines this change made for `voice_cue_types`, but it changes master cue behaviour on the recording stack and belongs in its own change.

## 470. A bounded fetch owes every surface it feeds a bound, and a drilldown that lists every row pays in row WIDTH, not in a window

**Date:** 2026-08-03

§ 332's fix (PR #447) bounded `/dashboard`'s run fetch to a ~2-year window and moved the two lifetime headline cards onto a cheap `fetchRunAllTimeStats` aggregate. What it did not do was tell the *other* consumer of that array that it was now bounded. `<PeriodSummary>` kept receiving `filteredRuns` and kept offering an "all time" tab and unbounded Previous paging — so the modal opened by the exact "Longest run / **all time**" stat card rolled up only the last 730 days and contradicted the card that opened it. Same for Total runs. The under-report is unbounded in magnitude: a runner's whole pre-window history, including a lifetime-longest run, simply wasn't in the sum, and paging Previous past the bound rendered a real month as empty rather than as unknown (issue #664).

**The bound is now a prop, not an assumption.** `periodNeedsFullHistory(type, periodStart, coveredFrom)` in `core/dashboard_runs.ts` — beside the window constant it is the counterpart to — answers whether a period can be served from the caller's set at all: `coveredFrom == null` means the caller holds the complete history and never re-fetches (the standalone `/dashboard/period` route), `'all'` can *never* be answered from a bounded set, and week/month reach out only when they start before the bound. The dashboard passes `dashboardRunsWindowStart(new Date())` plus a loader; the component fetches once, caches for its lifetime, and until it resolves shows a loading state rather than the windowed number. **Showing the truncated total and silently correcting it later was rejected**: a wrong number that looks settled is the failure mode this whole issue is, and the drilldown is a click, not a paint.

**The durable shape for a lifetime figure depends on whether the surface displays rows or a scalar.** Total runs and longest run are scalars, so they get a server-side aggregate and ship no rows at all — that is what #447 got right. The period drilldown *lists every run it counts*, so no aggregate can serve it and no window can either; it genuinely needs O(all runs) rows. The saving therefore had to come from row **width**: `PERIOD_SUMMARY_RUN_COLUMNS` is the five values the component renders, which drops the `metadata` jsonb bag — the single largest per-row cost and the actual weight behind § 332's complaint. The standalone `/dashboard/period` route, which was still on the unbounded `select('*')` `fetchRuns()`, moved onto the same narrowed reader, so the fix removes a scan rather than adding one. `fetchRunsForPeriodSummary` throws instead of degrading to `[]`, because a swallowed error on this surface renders as a total that is merely *short* — indistinguishable from the bug being fixed.

**The best-streak sub-label on the same page is the same class of defect and is deliberately NOT fixed here.** `computeRunStreaks(filteredRuns)` needs every distinct day the runner ever ran, and it is on the paint path, not behind a click — so neither a narrowed full-history fetch (still O(all runs) round trips on the highest-traffic page) nor a lazy load (there is no click to hang it on) is acceptable. The durable fix is a `run_streaks_for_user()` SQL aggregate returning `(current, best)` from a gaps-and-islands over the `(user_id, started_at)` index — one row, one round trip — mirroring how `gym_exercise_records` already serves all-time gym bests and how the identical CTE inside `award_achievements_for_user` already computes the streak-badge threshold. That needs a migration and is sequenced separately; `followups.md` tracks it, and it should read the *display*-side local-day convention rather than the awarder's UTC-date shortcut. A trigger-maintained cache under `derived_state.md` was considered and rejected: the query is an index-only scan over a few thousand rows, and a delete can *lower* a best streak, so a cache would buy nothing and owe an invariant.

## 471. The best-streak sub-label reads a local-day SQL aggregate that takes the source filter, and a failed fetch suppresses the claim

**Date:** 2026-08-03

The migration § 470 sequenced out: `run_streaks_for_user(p_tz, p_source)` (migration `20270501_001`) is the gaps-and-islands `(current, best)` aggregate over the `(user_id, started_at)` index — one row, one round trip on the paint path — and `/dashboard`'s streak card now derives its sub-label from it via `streak_card.ts#streakCardState`, with `computeRunStreaks` over the windowed fetch kept only as the pre-resolve headline. Three calls were open, all made here. **Day bucketing is the runner's local day, not the awarder's UTC shortcut**: the display-side `computeRunStreaks` keys days in client-local time, and two helpers that disagree on what "a day" is will disagree on whether a 23:30 run extends a streak — so the client passes its IANA zone (`Intl.DateTimeFormat().resolvedOptions().timeZone`, `at time zone` in SQL, DST-safe because date arithmetic steps calendar days). An unrecognized zone raises rather than silently bucketing wrong — but only when rows are actually scanned; a zero-run caller short-circuits to `(0,0)`, which the pgtap suite pins so nobody "fixes" the asymmetry into a validation pass. The awarder's UTC CTE stays as-is: a milestone threshold tolerates a day of skew, a displayed number beside "All-time best!" does not. **The RPC takes the source filter** rather than the card dropping its all-time claim under a filter: the streak card has always been scoped to the dashboard's source chips, the filter is one indexed predicate, and re-fetching per chip keeps the sub-label's claim true in every view — relabelling to "best in this view" would have kept a wrong number honest instead of making it right. **A failed fetch returns null, never zeros, and null suppresses the numeric claim.** `fetchRunAllTimeStats`' degrade-to-0 is survivable because a lifetime card reading 0 is visibly broken; a zeroed or windowed streak is indistinguishable from a truthful one — the § 470 failure mode — so `fetchRunStreaks` returns null on any error and `streakCardState` then renders no "Best: N"/"All-time best!" at all, falling back only to the claim-free restart/start lines the windowed data can prove. Mobile needs no twin for the fetch (its card reads the local store), but note the store only holds what was recorded on-device or paged in — a fresh install of a deep-history account under-reports the same way until history is paged in; that is a store-population question, not this RPC's, and is left open.

## 472. The master spoken-cues toggle follows the per-cue map to `UD`, and a corrupt value is dropped rather than read in either direction

**Date:** 2026-08-03

**Amends [§ 469](#469-the-per-cue-voice-map-becomes-ud-because-the-surface-that-edits-a-preference-is-not-the-surface-that-obeys-it)'s closing note**, which named `voice_feedback_enabled` as the same defect left unfixed: registered `D`, written by web's `/settings/preferences` to the universal bag, read by mobile only from the device bag — so the master toggle, unlike the per-cue map it gates, still never reached a phone. The fix is the four lines § 469 predicted: the key is `UD` in `settings.md`, `SettingsSyncService` reads it from both bags via one helper called from `_applyUniversal` and `_applyDevice`, and the existing universal-first-device-second apply order means a phone whose own switch has ever written the device bag keeps its per-phone choice (a race phone and a training phone can differ) while a phone that never touched it inherits the web value. Absent in both bags, the phone's local default — on — stands; no web change was needed because web has written the universal bag all along.

**The polarity call:** a non-bool bag value is dropped, never coerced — but for a MASTER gate the two coercion directions fail differently, so the choice is recorded. Coercing truthy could blast audio a runner explicitly muted; coercing falsy silently kills every spoken cue at once, including the cutoff catch-up and pace cues a racer may be depending on mid-effort, with no UI hint that anything changed. § 469's per-cue read only ever risks one cue per corrupt entry; here one corrupt value would take the whole voice layer, in whichever direction it coerced. Dropping does neither: the phone's last locally-known choice survives, which for a fresh install is the default-on and for everyone else is whatever they last chose on any surface that reached this phone. The sync-apply path stays a type-gated field write inside `onSignedIn`'s existing catch — nothing new can throw into the recording stack, whose TTS layer is already L4-isolated per cue.

## 473. The four planar frames outside § 468's scope get the same fold, and two of the survey's claims about them were wrong

**Date:** 2026-08-03

[§ 468](#468-the-antimeridian-fix-crosses-back-from-the-watch-to-web-and-mobile-and-the-normalisation-is-owned-once-per-platform) routed the five parity-pair modules through `geo` and deliberately left four sites carrying the raw longitude subtraction, because none is in the enforced lockstep set and each is a separate behaviour change. This closes all four — `routing_quality`'s projection frame, `nearest_track_point`'s bbox grid, `route_loop`'s synthetic-curve delta, and the run thumbnail's 5 m "worth drawing" span — under the same bar: the helpers are exact identities within a hemisphere, and not one existing pinned value moved (the web suite grew 3,150 → 3,160 by addition only; the touched Dart suites likewise).

**Sequencing them separately was right, and not only for reviewability — each had its own failure shape.** `routing_quality`'s frame read a point ON a segment crossing 180° as ~87 m off it, and a waypoint just across the line from the polyline as ~40,000 km off the snapped path — a spurious deviation warning on every antimeridian route. `nearest_track_point` was worse than the survey's "degenerates to a single column": with a ~359.9° span the cells come out ~2.8° wide, and beyond making every tap near-linear, the ring-termination proof (ring *r*+1 is at least *r*·minCell away) assumes a contiguous frame — across the line it is unsound, so a tap beside the meridian could settle on a ~430 m same-side vertex while the true nearest sat ~53 m away, 127 columns over. A wrong answer, not a slow one; a deterministic decoy test pins it, and the grid now carries a `refLng` every build and query unwraps against.

**Two survey claims did not survive contact.** followups.md called `route_loop` web-only; `route_loop.dart` exists, declares lockstep with the web module in its own file header, and carried the same defect — with a harder edge on mobile, where an interior waypoint flung past 180° trips `latlong2`'s debug-mode longitude assert, so Generate-by-distance across the line crashed a debug build outright. Both sides now fold the delta through `lonDeltaDeg` and wrap every emitted longitude (the loop branch too: a radial ring seeded beside the line used to emit lng 180.006). And the span check's "benign — a track across the line always reads as meaningful" was backwards in the only case the gate exists for: ~2 m of stationary jitter AT the line read as a 359.99° span and *passed* the 5 m gate, drawing exactly the meaningless one-pixel dot the check suppresses.

**The span check moved rather than being fixed inline.** It was untestable inside `RunTrackPreview.svelte`; it is now `isTrackRenderable` in `routes/track_projection.ts`, taking the Dart twin's name and its long-standing placement beside `projectTrack` in `track_preview.dart` — which widens that informal pair from one helper to two rather than minting a module. Nothing here is verified against a real GPS trace near 180°, the same host-tested-only rung § 468 claims.

## 474. The master voice toggle's default is ON on every surface, and the snapshot-save-era un-chosen `false` bags are left standing

**Date:** 2026-08-03

The open box from [§ 472](#472-the-master-spoken-cues-toggle-follows-the-per-cue-map-to-ud-and-a-corrupt-value-is-dropped-rather-than-read-in-either-direction)'s survey: the three surfaces disagreed on what an untouched `voice_feedback_enabled` means — the `settings.md` registry said `false`, web's `/settings/preferences` loaded `effective(..., false)` and showed the switch off, and the phone's `Preferences.audioCues` has been `?? true` since v1. **ON wins.** The phone is the only surface that speaks, it has defaulted on since the first release, and § 472 deliberately kept the absent-in-both sync path on the phone's local default — so a runner who never touched the toggle has always heard cues. Flipping phones to quiet would silently change live mid-training behaviour for every such runner; aligning the registry + web fallback to on changes no runtime behaviour anywhere — it makes the displayed switch stop contradicting the device it claims to describe. The rejected direction (off, on a "quiet by default" instinct) would only be defensible for a brand-new product; retrofitting it here would make the default flip itself the mid-race surprise § 472's polarity argument refused to risk. § 472's absent-in-both behaviour is unchanged and now agrees with the registry instead of contradicting it.

**The save-path investigation found real un-chosen `false` values in universal bags.** Today's `autoSave` coalesces only explicitly-changed keys into `updateUniversal`, and `applyPrefsChanges` merges rather than snapshots — the current path cannot persist an untouched fallback. But from the voice editor's introduction (2026-04-25, `b93ac3e7c`) until auto-save landed (2026-06-01, `0cf249db1`), the page's `handleSave()` snapshotted the whole form — including `voice_feedback_enabled: voiceFeedbackEnabled`, seeded from the very `false` fallback this change corrects — so any runner who pressed Save for ANY preference in that window wrote a `false` they never chose. Those values are indistinguishable from a genuinely chosen off, and since § 472's `UD` promotion they actively mute a phone whose own switch never wrote the device bag. **They are left standing:** scrubbing `voice_feedback_enabled: false` from universal bags would un-mute every runner who deliberately chose quiet — the worse coercion direction by § 472's own argument — and no heuristic separates the cohorts. The default flip changes nothing for them (a stored value always beats a fallback); web now truthfully shows their stored off, and flipping the switch on writes an explicit true that roams.

**The pin:** `VOICE_FEEDBACK_ENABLED_DEFAULT` in `settings/voice_cues.ts` is the single web-side default (the preferences page imports it — no inline literal), and `voice_cues.test.ts` now asserts four surfaces agree by reading source: the Dart field initialiser and `?? true` load fallback in `preferences.dart`, the web page's `effective(...)` call, and the `settings.md` registry row's default cell. A future drift on any of them is a failing web unit test, not a survey box.

## 475. The mobile streak card reads the same all-time aggregate as web, and a lower bound is folded, never walked back

**Date:** 2026-08-03

Closes the box [§ 471](#471-the-best-streak-sub-label-reads-a-local-day-sql-aggregate-that-takes-the-source-filter-and-a-failed-fetch-suppresses-the-claim)'s closing note left open: mobile's `_StreakRow` computed both figures from `LocalRunStore.summaryRuns` — on-device recordings plus whatever server pages had been fetched — so a fresh install of a deep-history account presented a best streak read off a ~50-row sliver as the all-time truth. The fix reuses `run_streaks_for_user` from mobile (`ApiClient.fetchRunStreaks`, null — never zeros — on any failure) rather than back-filling full history into the local store: the store is windowed by design, an unbounded backfill costs unbounded storage + network on the highest-traffic screen, and it would still be wrong between install and backfill-complete — while the RPC is one indexed row on the same source of truth web reads. The § 471 posture carries over intact via a new `streak_card` TS↔Dart parity pair (`streakCardState`, 7 mirror tests each): when the RPC has answered, its row drives headline and sub-label; when it hasn't — loading, offline, signed out (a guard keeps the SECURITY INVOKER RPC uncalled) — the card shows only what the resident runs prove, and the best/"all-time best" sub-label renders as nothing instead of a windowed number indistinguishable from truth. No strings changed: the existing labels simply became conditional on the source that can back them.

**One mobile-only divergence, deliberate:** web hands the RPC row straight to `streakCardState`; mobile folds it with the local compute first (`mergeAllTimeStreaks`, pointwise max, documented as outside the pair). On an offline-first client both figures are lower bounds over subsets of the true run-day set — the server misses just-recorded unsynced runs, the device misses unpaged history — and a streak is monotone in that set, so the max is the closest provable figure. Without the fold, the RPC answering after a fresh save would walk the just-run streak back a day: the same silent correction § 471 forbids, arriving from the opposite direction. **Timezone:** the RPC buckets by `p_tz` and Dart's `timeZoneName` is an abbreviation, so the device's IANA zone comes from the `flutter_timezone` plugin (`deviceIanaTimeZone`, added to both twin pubspecs); when the platform can't name a zone the helper degrades to an explicit `'UTC'` — web's exact `Intl`-failure fallback — rather than faking equivalence with a fixed offset that buckets DST-era history onto different days than the display compute. `p_source` is not passed: the mobile dashboard has no source chips, so the card's truth is the unfiltered history.

## 476. Selected chips resolve their label color per state — via a WidgetStateColor inside labelStyle, because that is the only thing RawChip resolves

**Date:** 2026-08-03

Issue #666 V1: both themes paired `ChipThemeData.selectedColor` with a same-luminance `labelStyle` color (light: ink on dusk, 1.45:1; dark: parchment on coral, 1.88:1), so every selected `FilterChip` read as a blank pill, and `runs_screen.dart` had noticed and forked local palette copies rather than fixing the theme (its comment cited a `ui_kit AppPalette` class that never existed — V17). The fix the ticket prescribed — `labelStyle` as a `WidgetStateTextStyle` — does not work: `RawChip` never resolves the style as a whole; it `merge`s it flat (which empties a `WidgetStateTextStyle`) and resolves only `effectiveLabelStyle.color` as a `WidgetStateProperty`. The state fork therefore lives on a `WidgetStateColor` *inside* `labelStyle`: selected resolves to `onPrimary` (parchment on dusk 11.0:1; midnight on coral 9.12:1), unselected keeps the existing pairing. `secondaryLabelStyle` was deleted — its only SDK reader is `ChoiceChip`'s selected state, which the resolved `labelStyle` now covers (so the audit's "13 broken ChoiceChip sites" were in fact already legible; only Filter/Raw chips were broken). `checkmarkColor` is pinned to the same on-color — the M3 default (`onSecondaryContainer`) is near-invisible on the overridden `selectedColor`, a gap the deleted fork had been quietly covering. The runs_screen fork and stale comment are gone; a ui_kit test resolves the theme exactly as `RawChip` does and asserts computed WCAG ratios >= 4.5 for label and checkmark in both brightnesses.

## 477. Status colors are theme tokens (`AppSemanticColors`), and the run-screen banners were re-based onto them because the scheme's own error pair also fails AA as a fill

**Date:** 2026-08-03

Issue #666 V2, plus the foundation of V3. The four mid-run alert banners carried hand-picked Tailwind hexes under `Colors.white` — off-route and GPS-lost at 3.76:1, weak-GPS at 3.19:1 — on the one screen read at arm's length mid-run. The audit's prescribed target (`colorScheme.error` / `onError`) turned out to fail the same bar: white over `#D8594C` is 3.85:1, parchment 3.48:1, and the dark tone ~3.4:1 — the 47 files "using it correctly" use it as a *foreground on surfaces*, which proves nothing about it as a fill. Retuning the global error color would ripple through all 47, so the banners instead ride a new `AppSemanticColors` `ThemeExtension` (`success`/`warning`/`danger`/`crown` + `on*`, distinct light and dark instances): all three failure banners share the `danger` pair (permission-revoked had been a *third* red that happened to pass), weak-GPS takes `warning`. Every pair is pinned by a ui_kit test that computes WCAG relative luminance from the registered theme — >= 4.5:1 for each `on*`/base, >= 3:1 for each base against its scaffold — and a source guard bans the old hexes from `run_screen.dart` outright. The tree-wide V3 sweep (228 status-role hex literals across 43 files) deliberately did not start here: the extension is the token vocabulary it will migrate onto, and mixing a 43-file sweep into the banner fix would have buried the behaviour change.

## 478. Create/edit forms arm a shared discard guard that probes dirtiness at pop time, not at build time

**Date:** 2026-08-03

Issue #666 U1: ten form surfaces (the eight `showFullScreenForm` sheets plus the route builder and manual run entry) lost everything on an Android back gesture with no prompt — the app had three `PopScope`s total and none on a form. The shared fix is `widgets/confirm_discard.dart`: `confirmDiscard(context)` (the privacy-zones discard dialog lifted to generic copy, with an optional surface-specific body) and `DiscardGuard`, a `PopScope` wrapper that holds `canPop: false` and probes `isDirty()` **when the pop is requested**, popping only on confirmation. Build-time `canPop` — the ticket's sketch — goes stale by construction: most form edits live in `TextEditingController`s, which never rebuild the route, so a dirty form would slip out unguarded; the price of the pop-time probe is losing Android's predictive-back preview on guarded screens, which a data-loss guard is worth. `showFullScreenForm` gained an optional `isDirty` hook (null keeps prior behaviour byte-for-byte), each sheet wires a real predicate probed through a `GlobalKey` (the shower functions own no form state), and explicit Cancel buttons route through `Navigator.maybePop` so they meet the same guard — while save-success pops bypass it, the work being persisted. Predicates compare against the loaded entity (edit) or defaults (create), down to un-committed sub-editors (a typed-but-unadded gear wear-log note arms the guard); the nutrition sheet's search query and meal-slot pick deliberately do not (ephemeral, one tap to recreate). The web half of the audit item — the matching navigation guard on web forms — is not in this round and stays tracked on #666.

## 479. Offline-store pending rows are disclosed from `pendingCount`, never from connectivity

**Date:** 2026-08-03

Issue #666 U2: a gym workout, meal, gear item or routine whose push the server *rejected* (RLS, 500, expired token — anything but airplane mode) sat on disk pending forever while the screen showed it saved; the only banners were gated on `!_isOnline`, so being online hid the failure, and all 19 `syncWithServer` call sites discarded the drained count its own doc comment says to surface. The shared `PendingSyncBanner` renders from the stores' `pendingCount` (a getter added beside `hasPending`; no on-disk change): nothing pending renders nothing; pending while offline or signed out says saved-on-device-will-sync; pending while online says N-changes-haven't-synced with a Retry wired to `syncWithServer` on every passed store. Retry never clears optimistically — the drain returns, the spinner stops, and the banner re-renders from what is actually still pending — and per-row failure isolation is unchanged. The old connectivity-gated banners were replaced, not stacked: they survive only for the offline-with-nothing-pending "showing cached data" case the new banner deliberately does not cover, so at most one banner shows. Mounted on gym, nutrition, gear, routine-library, routine-detail, and gym-detail (whose save-as-routine drain was also discarded; it passes both its stores), with the `_maybeSync` helpers now consuming the returned count per the store's contract. Copy says "change(s)", not the audit's "item(s)" — pending rows include edits and delete tombstones, for which "item saved" would lie. The runs surface already did all of this and is untouched.

## 480. Every mobile status-role color literal migrated onto `AppSemanticColors`, with the ban pinned by a count-pinned source guard

**Date:** 2026-08-04

The round-1 extension (§477) stopped *new* status hexes; issue #666 V3 swept the legacy ones — 137 occurrences (87 hex + 50 `Colors.green/amber/red` swatches) across 41 files, of which 100 moved onto `success`/`warning`/`danger`/`crown` + their `on*` (the audit's "228" overcounted against its own hex list). `AppSemanticColors.ofTheme(ThemeData)` was added for context-free helpers, and the named drift unified: pace fast/slow, adherence-completed, gear-due, and the two crown golds — plus star/featured/rating golds — onto `crown`. The line drawn: a color that *communicates state on a theme surface* is a status role and takes a token; a color that *is data* — pace ramps, heat scales, HR/intensity zone bands, chart series, cartographic markers (start/finish caps, builder pins, hover/coarse dots) — is not, keeps its fixed hue, and is exempted by an exact-occurrence-count allowlist entry in `status_color_literal_guard_test.dart` (both twins), alongside the three whole-file share-card exemptions that rasterise to theme-free PNGs. Count-pinning means a new literal in an exempted file still fails and a migrated palette forces its entry's removal, so the allowlist can only shrink. `colorScheme.error`/`errorContainer` usages stay: they are theme tokens, legitimate as foreground/tonal pairs per §477 — the ban is on raw literals, not on Material's own scheme.

## 481. Hardcoded white foregrounds over theme-varying fills are replaced by role-paired scheme colors; identity avatars get a contrast-clamped shared widget

**Date:** 2026-08-04

`colorScheme.primary` flips from dusk `#3A2E5C` (light) to coral `#F2A07B` (dark), so a hardcoded `Colors.white` foreground that reads 11:1 in light collapses to ~2:1 in dark — the issue #666 V4 audit found four real sites among 92 white/black literals. Fixes pair fill and foreground by role, never by literal: the upcoming-event icon bubble uses `onPrimary` over `primary`; the solo-safety nudge drops its off-palette `#1F2937` slab for `inverseSurface`/`onInverseSurface` (the Material snackbar idiom — high-emphasis in both themes, body ≥10:1), with secondary text at `onInverseSurface` alpha 0.75 because 0.7 blends to a knife-edge 4.48–4.50:1 in dark; and the four hand-rolled HSL initial avatars (white on `HSLColor(hue, ~0.5, 0.55)`, ~2:1 at yellow/lime hues) are replaced by ui_kit's `IdentityAvatar`, which keeps the historical seed→hue hash byte-for-byte (no recoloring of already-legible hues), nudges lightness out of the mid-luminance band only when neither white nor ink reaches 4.5:1, and picks the foreground by computed luminance — pinned by a 360-hue AA sweep. The superseded `hashHue`/`initialFor` helpers were deleted from `social_service.dart` (ui_kit's suite pins the identical algorithm). Tests assert scheme roles and computed contrast in both themes, not hex literals, so a future palette change can't silently reintroduce the class.

## 482. Dusk component themes: buttons share one silhouette, cards separate by hairline not tint, and labelSmall is the micro-label floor

**Date:** 2026-08-04

Round 3 of the issue #666 audit moved three per-site conventions into `AppTheme` (both brightnesses). Every button family (Filled/Elevated/Outlined/Text) now themes to the radius-12 rounded rectangle with 14px vertical padding, so a primary and its paired secondary match in shape and height without call-site styling. `cardTheme` gives cards `elevation: 0`, a `colorScheme.surface` fill, and a 1px hairline in the brightness's divider token — chosen over M3's `surfaceContainerLow` because the seeded light value (`#F8F2FA`) computes to 1.005:1 against parchment and carries a cool-lavender cast on the warm page, so tonal separation is simply unavailable in light, while dark gets a real 1.174:1 step from `duskDeep` plus the same hairline for one mechanism everywhere. `textTheme.labelSmall` pins 11px/w500 as the declared micro-label floor, and the sub-11 `fontSize:` overrides were raised onto the token. Card interiors standardize on two insets — `all(16)` for content blocks, `fromLTRB(16,12,16,12)` for list rows (right 8 when the row ends in a bare IconButton) — and per-site Card `elevation:` args are gone (the audit's "12 of 220" was 2 — the rest were non-Card widgets); deliberately theme-free surfaces (rasterised share cards, map overlay chips/pills) keep bespoke values.

## 483. Gym-session drafts resume by replaying the runner, and the in-flight snapshot rides the draft row's metadata, not a separate file

**Date:** 2026-08-04

A live guided gym session could be popped by one back gesture: the 10 s durable save preserved the sets as an orphan `gym_workouts` row, but runner state (current step, elapsed) was unrecoverable (issue #666 U5). The pop is now guarded by a three-way dialog (keep going / leave — draft kept / discard) shared with the band's Abandon control — `DiscardGuard` (§478) was deliberately not reused because the session's leave outcome is ternary and non-destructive, though its pop-time-probe shape is mirrored — and the durable save stamps a `gym_session_draft` metadata key (registered in metadata.md) carrying the ordered per-step outcome list, so a force-kill is as resumable as a graceful leave. Unlike the run side's separate in-progress file, the snapshot rides the already-syncing draft row: one recovery artifact, no second store, at the cost of the key transiently reaching the server until finish replaces the metadata bag. Resume (a gym-screen card mirroring run's Resume/Finish/Discard) rebuilds the runner by replaying the outcomes through its public API — the current step is derived, never stored, so an edited routine degrades to replay-what-fits — and elapsed re-anchors to `now − saved duration_s`, continuing from the last save rather than billing the gap, matching `resumeSession` on the run side. The same round localized the run-detail adherence pill (web already was) and finished the devices override registry's key-not-string conversion (badges idiom), deleting its residual English fallback literals.

## 484. Transient mutation failures banner with a Retry action; validation renders as per-field errorText, not a form-level string

**Date:** 2026-08-04

Round 4 of the issue #666 audit (U8/U9/U6) set two mobile error-surface conventions. First: a TRANSIENT mutation failure (sync, post/reply, join/leave, result submit, safety-contact write, coach turn/archive) surfaces through `showTopBanner` with an `errorStateRetry` action that re-invokes the failed mutation — the confirm-gated flows split the mutation out (`_doLeave`, `_doArchive`, `_submitPickedResult`) so Retry re-runs the operation, never the dialog — while inline `errorContainer` strips are reserved for LOAD failures (club detail keeps its strip for `_load` only; the coach screen's strip is gone). Retry closures capture the failed call's arguments (the picked result, the reply's post id) so retrying is faithful, and text inputs keep their content on failure so a re-submit sends exactly what was typed; failures that would duplicate state on a blind re-send (mid-SSE stream errors) banner without a retry. Second: form validation follows the sign_up_screen idiom — computed in ONE pass on save, rendered as `errorText` on the offending field's decoration, cleared when that field changes, save gated on the same predicate — applied to all six form sheets; the club and event forms previously ignored an empty name/title silently. A form-level error string remains only for genuinely cross-field conditions (goal editor's no-target) and for save failures, where the adjacent Save button is already the retry affordance.

## 485. Empty surfaces share ui_kit's EmptyState, and the run screen's top overlays compose as one Column

**Date:** 2026-08-04

Round 4 of the issue #666 audit closed the two remaining visual findings. V9: empty screens had no shared primitive the way errored ones have `ErrorState`, so 14 sites drifted on icon size (64/56/none), padding (32/16/none — gear ran its text to the screen edge), and CTA presence; `EmptyState` in `packages/ui_kit` now reuses ErrorState's icon size (48) and `all(32)` padding — adding its own titleMedium title + bodySmall body split and optional CTA — and adapts to its host — under bounded height it fills, centres, and stays scrollable for pull-to-refresh hosts; under unbounded height (embedded in an outer scrollable, e.g. nutrition's meal list) it renders bare content so a nested always-scrollable can't eat the host's drags. It lives in ui_kit rather than beside ErrorState because it takes plain strings and needs no l10n dependency. V10: the run screen's top overlays were pinned at literal `top:` offsets, so off-route + GPS-lost (independent sources) drew on the same top-60 band and the centred cards crossed the top-56 badges; the top band now composes as ONE Positioned Column — the badge row, then `RunTopBanners` (off-route, the permission/GPS else-if chain, the safety nudge) — the same treatment the bottom-anchored utility stack already got, with `RunTopBanners` public so the stacking is pinned by a widget test (non-overlapping Rects) without pumping the map screen.

## 486. Overflow-prone rows are bound by Expanded/ellipsis or reflowed by OverflowBar, with an explicit exemption taxonomy

**Date:** 2026-08-04

Round 5 of the issue #666 audit closed V7 (unbounded `Text` in `Row`, ~107 candidate sites) across `lib/widgets/` and `lib/screens/` with three mechanisms, chosen per row shape. A localized LABEL sharing a row gets `Expanded`/`Flexible` + `maxLines: 1` + `TextOverflow.ellipsis` (the label truncates, never the value). An END-ALIGNED action row (sheet Cancel/Save, composer Post, photo upload/caption rows) becomes an `OverflowBar` so long German/French button labels stack instead of striping. A row that must keep OPPOSING ends (event detail's DNF/DNS pair vs Cancel, the setup wizard's Back vs Skip/Continue, dashboard's empty-state CTA pair) puts the grouped side in an `Expanded(Wrap)` so the opposite anchor survives the reflow. Fixes are pinned by narrow-width tests (320px typical, 220px for the safety banner) — worth their cost: the route_conditions pin caught two residual overflows the first pass had missed. Just as load-bearing is what was deliberately NOT bound, so a later sweep doesn't "finish" these: short numeric/stat values riding beside an `Expanded` sibling (times, distances, counts — the value side is already the bounded side); chip rows inside a horizontal `SingleChildScrollView` (bounded by scroll); the fixed-canvas share rasterisers (theme-free PNG class, §480); framework-managed internals (`SegmentedButton`, `NavigationRail`, `PopupMenuItem`); and any label beside an `Expanded` sibling where `Flexible` would cap that sibling at its flex share — Flutter does not redistribute loose-fit leftover, so "bounding" the exercise-catalogue picker's category label would have shrunk the dropdown in the common case. Corrections to the audit text: `run_screen.dart:4806` resolves to the paused-controls row of fixed 52–56px icon circles whose only texts are a lap badge and short numerics, so the live recording screen was left untouched (layered resilience, §24 of conventions); and the audit's per-file counts predate rounds 1–4, whose refits had already absorbed several listed sites.

## 487. Dusk finishes its component themes: one line token at 3:1, a scrolled-under app bar, a bottom-sheet contract, one field language, and cards that do not inset themselves

**Date:** 2026-08-04

Round 6 of the issue #666 audit landed the four theme-level edits round 3 (§482) left open plus the card-margin sweep, all in `AppTheme`'s two getters. **Lines (S5):** `parchmentDim` on parchment computes to 1.135:1 and `duskDivider` on duskDeep to 1.129:1 — the audit's 1.13:1 for both is right, and it means the §482 card hairline, the mechanism that was supposed to separate a light card from the page, has been invisible since it shipped. Worse, three names were doing one job: 46 `theme.dividerColor` reads (33 of them `Border.all`, matching the audit), 43 `Divider`s plus a `VerticalDivider` (which under M3 ignore `dividerColor` and resolve `colorScheme.outlineVariant` — a *different* grey, 1.543:1 light / 1.728:1 dark), and 15 explicit `outlineVariant` borders, not the 8 the audit counted. The fix is one token per brightness — `parchmentLine` `#8A806A` (hue-matched to parchment at H40, 3.53:1 on parchment, 3.11:1 on parchmentDim) and `duskLine` `#786A9A` (H257, the hue every violet in the palette already sits on, 3.33:1 on duskDeep and 3.91:1 on midnight) — pinned simultaneously as `dividerColor`, `dividerTheme.color` and a `colorScheme.outlineVariant` override, which is why all 105 sites moved without a single call-site edit. The card outline deliberately follows the token rather than staying soft: in light the card fill *is* the scaffold colour, so the hairline is the only boundary and therefore is exactly the "visual information required to identify a UI component" that SC 1.4.11 sets at 3:1; leaving it below that while raising dividers would have re-created the drift the finding is about. Text keeps a separate, higher bar — `run_detail_screen.dart`'s elevation-chart labels still take `onSurfaceVariant` and were left alone (the line token is 3.53:1, still short of AA for text); only that comment's parenthetical "~#E0E0E0" was ever wrong, never its conclusion.

**App bars (C3):** both brightnesses paired `elevation: 0` with `scrolledUnderElevation: 0` over a background equal to the scaffold, and with zero `SliverAppBar`/`NestedScrollView` in the tree that made all ~70 screens a flat 56dp band with content sliding invisibly beneath. M3's own mechanism is unusable here for the same reason §482 rejected `surfaceContainerLow`: the seeded tint is `#64558F`, which over parchment at the elevation-3 opacity computes to `#E7E2E2` — 1.16:1 *and* a cool cast on a warm page. `AppBar` resolves `AppBarThemeData.backgroundColor` through `WidgetStateProperty.resolveAs` against a state set containing `scrolledUnder`, so the durable fix is a `WidgetStateColor`: light rises parchment → parchmentDim (1.135:1) and adds a real shadow (`scrolledUnderElevation: 3` with `shadowColor: ink`, since M3's AppBar default is a transparent shadow), dark rises midnight → dusk (1.559:1, against 1.224:1 for the tint and 1.174:1 for duskDeep) and carries the whole separation in the fill because no shadow is visible against a `#120D22` page. A 1.135:1 step is deliberately below the hairline bar and above M3's own default (`surfaceContainer`, 1.050:1): a 56dp band and a 1px line are not the same perceptual problem.

**Bottom sheets (C10):** 31 `showModalBottomSheet` sites shared no presentation — 7 drew a drag handle, 1 set a shape, none agreed on a background. `bottomSheetTheme` now owns background (`colorScheme.surface`, tint disabled), the top radius 20 the single shaped site had already chosen, the drag handle in the line token, and `clipBehavior`. `useSafeArea` is not a theme field and could not be folded in; rather than invent a wrapper around a one-line argument, the rule became `isScrollControlled: true` implies `useSafeArea: true` — the cap on a non-scroll-controlled sheet is 9/16 of the screen, so only scroll-controlled sheets can reach the status bar at all — and a source guard fails the pair. It caught three sites the manual sweep missed. The four transparent share sheets opt out of the handle explicitly: they host their own rasterisable card and a handle would float over the scrim.

**Fields (S12):** the audit's "M3 filled-underline" is a misnomer — `filled` defaults to false, so those sheets rendered a bare underline. The theme names the outlined language at radius 12 (matching §482's button silhouette; `people_screen` had already picked 12 by hand), and 70 per-site `OutlineInputBorder()` declarations were deleted so they inherit it instead of re-pinning Material's default radius 4 — well past the 24 in the form-sheet family, because leaving the rest at 4 would have kept the drift under a different name. Only `border:` was removed: `isDense` and explicit `contentPadding` are load-bearing on the inline dense fields and were left, as were the five deliberately different components (two filled borderless search boxes, a radius-20 chat composer, a radius-999 pill). Nothing needed doing for error state — with only `border` set, `InputDecorator` resolves the error/focus outline from `defaults.outlineBorder`, so §486's `errorText` work still reads.

**Cards (C1):** the audit's three left edges (16 / 20 / 32) are real and `mileage_trend_card.dart` carries a field report from an earlier round about exactly this ("the Mileage modal looks less wide than the other modals"). Its prescription — `margin: EdgeInsets.zero` on the card theme — was **not** taken, because it assumes the blast radius is the four bespoke margins: in fact 49 of the 92 `Card(` sites name no margin at all and were taking Material's `EdgeInsets.all(4)` as their only stacked separation, several of them (club-detail's pending-request loop, the run screen's stacked alert banners, list-tile cards in builders) in files owned by other slices of this same round. The card theme therefore takes `EdgeInsets.symmetric(vertical: 4)`: zero horizontally kills the entire drift class — a card's left edge is now its parent's padding edge and nothing else, app-wide, with no collateral edits — while the vertical 4 preserves every stacked-card site untouched. The four bespoke margins are gone and the dashboard's chart stack falls to a uniform 8dp rhythm (it was 8/12/16/16). The pinning test measures each card's **Material descendant**, not the `Card` element: a `Card`'s own render object spans its margin box, so a first attempt that measured the element passed even with a 16dp horizontal margin injected — the guard was verified by injecting one and watching it fail.
## 488. Planning gets a destination: a labelled in-body peer strip on the run and gym surfaces, not a sixth nav slot

**Date:** 2026-08-04

Round 6 of the issue #666 audit closed one root cause behind five findings. The five bottom-nav slots cover Review (twice), Capture, Social and Manage; **Plan gets none**, so every planning tool had been filed under whichever surface owned its *data*: routes and training plans hung off the run history list as two tooltip-only `IconButton`s, gym routines and records off the gym log's AppBar the same way, the race calendar off an API-vendor tile in Settings, and session plans nowhere at all. The fix is the one web already shipped and needs no sixth slot: a labelled in-body strip of peer surfaces — `Runs · Routes · Plans · Races` on the run surface (mirroring `RunSurfaceTabs.svelte`) and `Log · Routines · Sessions · Records` on the gym surface (mirroring `/gym`'s header links) — extracted once as `widgets/surface_peer_strip.dart` and mounted at both call sites, the run one fed by a new `RunsScreen.surfacePeers` (which replaces the deleted `onOpenRoutes` / `onOpenPlans` callbacks; the hub was their only caller) and the gym one built internally since `GymScreen` already owns every store it needs. It is a horizontally-scrollable `ChoiceChip` row — text only, no avatar, so the M3 checkmark carries the selected state alongside the fill and no icon competes for the leading slot; the current peer is the selected chip with a null `onTap`, so it stays focusable and announces as selected instead of being disabled; scroll bounds it rather than `Expanded`/ellipsis because a peer name truncated to "Trainingspl…" is not a name (the §486 exemption for chip rows inside a horizontal scroll view, taken deliberately). `routes_screen.dart`'s existing labelled Discover strip was read first and left alone: it fans out to *sub-surfaces* of Routes and has no current-peer concept, so generalising the two into one widget would have merged two different jobs. The strip subsumes and deletes four icon-only AppBar actions (Routes, Plans, Routines, Records) — both affordances were never kept side by side. Two reachability holes closed with it: `RacesScreen` had exactly one instantiation app-wide, from two Settings → Integrations tiles each `onTap`-gated on `_runSignUpAvailable` / `_chronoTrackAvailable`, so a deployment with **neither provider key had zero reachable entry points** to a full search / distance-band / geocode / crowd-submission surface — the probe governs the per-race *import*, never the public search RPC, so both tiles are now unconditionally tappable, disclose the import status in their subtitle and the destination on a second line (using the two already-translated `integrations*Open` keys that had shipped unused), and both entry points now pass the MapTiler key that "near a place" needs and that the Settings path had never threaded; and `SessionsScreen` had no instantiation at all outside its own declaration and test, so a user could open a *club's* session plan from club detail but never reach their own list. Corrections to the audit text: every line number in it predates rounds 1–5 and had drifted (`runs_screen.dart:1114-1125` is now `1124-1135`, `gym_screen.dart:236-247` is now `374-392`, `settings_integrations_screen.dart:247` still resolves); `races_screen.dart`'s header comment claiming it is "reached as a sub-route from the run surface" was false when written and is now true, so it was corrected rather than deleted. Landing the strip also exposed a pre-existing §486-class overflow the audit had not caught: `PendingSyncBanner`'s Retry sat at the tail of the message `Row`, and a `TextButton` takes its intrinsic width before the `Expanded` message gets any, so the German "Erneut versuchen" starved the text to a few pixels and grew the banner to 544 px — invisible until the strip's 64 px of chrome pushed the gym body's `Column` 24 px past a 320 dp viewport. The action now reflows onto its own end-aligned line, pinned by a 320 dp German test on the banner and on the gym screen.
## 489. Chart keys name the colour their plot draws, the elevation pace ramp separates by luminance, and the map-style preference finally resolves the basemap

**Date:** 2026-08-04

Round 6 of the issue #666 audit closed the three "the UI asserts something untrue" findings. **(1) Training load.** The legend recoloured the Form key by `sign(tsb)` — `AppSemanticColors.success` above zero, `danger` below — while `_ChartPainter` drew that series in a fixed `#EF4444`, so a tapered runner (TSB ≥ 0, the state the card exists to celebrate) read a green key over a red line. Of the two fixes the audit floated, segmenting the stroke by sign was rejected: a legend key names a *series*, not a state, so a two-toned line leaves the single swatch ambiguous, and over a 90-day window at 180 px the sign flips would render as 1–2 px fragments. The Form series takes one fixed hue in both places instead — the sign is already told three other ways on the same card (the painter forces zero into the value range specifically so the dashed zero line shows it, the legend entry prints the signed number, and the reading chip says loaded/balanced/tapered). Colouring a *data series* by status was also a §480 category error. Hoisting all three hues to one constant each, read by both the legend and the painter, **shrinks** the guard's data-palette entry from `{F59E0B: 2, EF4444: 1}` to `{F59E0B: 1, EF4444: 1}`, which is the direction §480 requires. Web carried the identical defect (`.form.positive .swatch { background: #10b981 }` against `.line.form { stroke: #ef4444 }`) and was fixed in the same commit so the mobile file's "mirrors TrainingLoadChart.svelte" claim stays true. **(2) Elevation pace bands.** The audit's figures were stale — its `#B3E8CF`/`#F7C6C1` composites are the *pre-§480 Tailwind* palette over pure white, and the real numbers are worse: composited over the actual page background the current bands give faster-vs-slower **1.026:1 in light** (audit said 1.12) and **1.104:1 in dark** (audit said 1.17). The replacement drops alpha entirely — the painter and the new three-key legend read the same opaque `Color` list, so they cannot drift the way (1) did — and separates the bands by luminance rather than hue: light `#89BF9D` / `#9E702E` / `#7C3024` (adjacent 2.08:1 and 2.09:1, extremes 4.34:1, each ≥ 1.90:1 against parchment) and dark `#325D42` / `#B47F34` / `#EFCDC7` (adjacent 2.17:1 and 2.36:1, extremes 5.12:1, each ≥ 2.51:1 against midnight). Because a WCAG ratio is computed from relative luminance alone, those floors *are* greyscale-separation floors, which is what makes the encoding survive red-green colour-vision deficiency; a strict-monotonicity test pins the ordering the ratios alone would allow to fold. Pairwise 3:1 across all three was measured and rejected as unreachable — it forces the extreme pair past 9:1, which over midnight (L = 0.005) needs a near-white band and over parchment a band 1.4:1 from the page. Slower always sits furthest from the background, so "heavier ink is slower" holds in both themes even as the ramp direction inverts with the background — the same inversion `AppSemanticColors` already performs. The unpaceable segments keep the faintest fill of all four (`onSurface` at 0.08) and stay out of the legend: that band is an absence, not a fourth category. **(3) Map style.** Settings offered four basemaps and persisted the pick since launch, and nothing read it back. `resolveTileUrl` now takes `mapStyle` + `brightness` and ports web's `buildMapStyleUrl` slug switch verbatim (`satellite`, `outdoor-v2`, `streets-v2-dark`, and `streets` following the app theme), with the `TILE_URL_TEMPLATE` override still outranking everything (§68) and the keyless OSM fallback unchanged. The preference reaches the seven map surfaces the way `preferred_unit` does — mirrored from the universal bag into `Preferences.mapStyle` (so it survives a cold start offline) and read context-free through `activeMapStyle` — because none of those widgets carries a `Preferences` dep; an unknown value normalises to `streets` rather than blanking the map, and sign-out resets it with the other account-scoped mirrors. Overlays derive from the **resolved basemap**, not the app theme, since the OSM fallback is light whatever the theme is and a `dark` preference is dark inside the light theme: the casing flips between `#1E1B4B` and white (it computed to **1.08:1** against a representative `streets-v2-dark` land fill — on the dark basemap every map was locked to, the casing did nothing at all — and reads 13.93:1 and 15.54:1 respectively once flipped), and the legacy track gradient gets a second ramp because its pale `#C7D2FE` tail computes to **1.30:1** over an OSM light fill; both ramps now start at `#6366F1` and move away from the basemap, every stop ≥ 3.85:1. Satellite counts as dark (imagery is mid-to-low luminance); an override is treated as light unless its URL names a dark style, because `bin/protomaps-dev.sh` serves the light `basic` style. Two corrections to the audit here. Its "white marker fills" claim does not survive computation: the distance pin's white fill is 1.09–1.15:1 against a light basemap but its `#4F46E5` border is 5.48–5.75:1, and on a dark basemap the fill is 17.19:1 — the boundary clears 3:1 in both directions via complementary halves of the same pin, so it was left alone. What genuinely assumed a dark basemap is the white *separator ring* on the coloured dots (pulsing position, chart-hover, course markers), which vanishes at 1.09:1 on a light map and now takes the same flipped outline as the casing. Left deliberately unchanged and reported instead: the `#F59E0B` overlays (selected segment, coarse-position ring, hover fill) sit at 1.87–1.96:1 against a light basemap — a real finding, but outside this slice's scope and inside §480's count-pinned data-palette entry. Share cards are pinned to the dark basemap regardless of theme or preference: they rasterise a fixed dark PNG whose white type would otherwise land on a light map. Basemap-representative land fills (`#F2EFE9`, `#1A1B20`) are declared as samples in the test file, not as facts — a basemap is many colours, and the floors only claim "this overlay separates from the map at all".
## 490. Deep links name a profile tab, and version / update / legal live under About, not Licenses

**Date:** 2026-08-04

Round 6 of the issue #666 audit closed the structural findings from rounds 3 and 4, including the audit's one confirmed functional bug. I2: `notification_bell` pushed `ProfileScreen(initialTab: 3)` against a comment describing a four-tab profile, but a Badges tab had since been inserted ahead of the others, making Notifications index 4 — and because `_tabCount` was 5 the stale literal was in range, so the clamp never caught it and every bell tap landed the user on their **Following** list. The durable seam is a `ProfileTab` enum plus a single `_tabOrder` getter that the TabBar labels, the TabBarView children, and the deep-link index all read, so inserting a tab can no longer silently re-point a link; a tab the profile does not carry (Notifications on someone else's) resolves to the first tab rather than a numerically nearby one, since clamping an absent tab to its neighbour is how the original bug read as working. I1: the app's only version display and only Play in-app-update path sat behind a tile labelled "Licenses" under "Account & legal", where nobody looking to update would find them, and the update check fired from `initState` on every visit to a legal page; the screen is now `settings_about_screen.dart` — About & updates — ordered version, then an explicit on-demand "Check for updates" action, then an Open-source licenses row pushing `showLicensePage`. I4: despite that section heading, a signed-in user had no route to the Privacy Policy, Terms, Cookie notice or health-data notice — the only links in the app were pre-account, inline in `sign_up_screen`. A shared `legal_links.dart` (`LegalDoc` enum + `openLegalDoc`) now backs both, so the sign-up consent gate and the About screen open the same four documents web lists in its settings nav footer (§243) from one definition rather than a duplicated URL literal. The same round made two empty states actionable — nutrition targets stopped telling mobile users to go set body metrics "on the web app" for a screen that has shipped on mobile since G5, and gym records grew the CTA that fills it — and replaced club detail's hand-rolled error block with the shared `ErrorState`, deleting its bespoke retry string.

## 491. Every map credits the basemap it actually resolved to, a dead tile reads as map rather than as a hole, and one projection draws every track thumbnail

**Date:** 2026-08-04

Round 7 of the issue #666 audit closed the map layer's honesty findings. **(1) Attribution.** `flutter_map` renders none — unlike web, where MapLibre's attribution control reads the string straight out of the style.json and has been doing so all along (the keyless path too: `apps/web/static/osm-fallback-style.json` declares the OSM credit on its source) — so seven mobile surfaces displayed MapTiler and OpenStreetMap tiles crediting neither. That is an unfinished look and a basemap-ToS gap in one: MapTiler Cloud requires "© MapTiler" on screen whenever a map is displayed, linked, and "© OpenStreetMap contributors" alongside it wherever OSM data is underneath, which for us is every style we resolve to — MapTiler's own guidance draws no satellite exception, and their satellite style's labels are OSM-derived anyway; the OSM raster fallback owes the ODbL credit on its own account. The credit therefore cannot be a fixed string, because since § 489 the basemap varies with the map-style preference, the app theme, and the `TILE_URL_TEMPLATE` override: `basemapCreditsFor(env)` branches on exactly the precedence `resolveTileUrl` uses, so the keyed path names MapTiler + OpenStreetMap, the keyless raster fallback names OpenStreetMap alone, and an override names Protomaps + OpenStreetMap (the documented target is `bin/protomaps-dev.sh`, whose PMTiles are built from OSM — an override pointed at non-OSM data would make that credit wrong, and the fix is to grow the branch, not to leave the map crediting the wrong party). Wording mirrors web's own `licenseList` map-data section rather than being invented. Proper nouns stay untranslated and travel as identifiers; the sentence around them is localized in all seven ARBs, because "contributors" is a word and OSM's own guidance invites translating it. The strip anchors to the bottom **start** rather than the bottom-right MapLibre defaults to on web, because every locate / re-centre control in the app is a `FloatingActionButton` and Material anchors those to the end — a credit a floating button sits on top of is not a credit. Ink and scrim key off the resolved basemap for the same reason the casing does — white over a dark map, `#1E1B4B` over a light one, on a translucent slab opaque enough that the worst patch the opposite-luminance map can paint (a snow field under the dark scrim, tarmac under the light) still holds the text above 4.5:1, so legibility rests on the scrim rather than on a basemap we cannot enumerate. A guard enumerates every `FlutterMap` in `lib/` and fails if the set drifts from the seven files each asserted to mount the credit, so attribution is a property of *being a map*, not a per-screen nicety. **The share cards get it too**: they rasterise to a PNG that leaves the device, which is precisely the case MapTiler's static-image clause covers. **`MissingMapTilesHint` was deliberately left on its one screen** rather than spread to the other six: it is a developer instruction naming an env var and a file path, and repeating a hardcoded-English banner six times multiplies the English, not the diagnosis — the user-facing half of what it said ("you are on the OSM fallback") is now told on all seven by the credit strip, which names OpenStreetMap alone exactly when that is true. **(2) Tile failures.** The audit's "a failed tile is a hole showing the scaffold" is imprecise and the real number is worse in one direction and better in another: `flutter_map` paints its own `#E0E0E0` under every layer, so the gap was never the scaffold — it was a **13.02:1** light-grey rectangle against the dark basemap all seven maps were locked to before § 489. `basemapVoidColour` keys that backdrop to the resolved basemap (1.12:1 and 1.13:1 against the respective land samples — a void that *blends* is the point), `EvictErrorTileStrategy.notVisibleRespectMargin` stops a 404 being cached as a permanent gap so panning back re-requests it, and `errorTileCallback` logs the first failure then every hundredth so a flaky network cannot drown the log the recording stack writes to. No `errorImage`: a broken-glyph tiled across the viewport is a worse failure surface than a map-coloured void, and it would ship an asset whose only job is to be seen when something is wrong. All seven now build their raster layer through one `basemapTileLayer`, and the guard pins that the app contains exactly one bare `TileLayer(` — the factory itself. **(3) The spark painter.** `_TrackSparkPainter` on the run screen scaled latitude and longitude by one factor while its sibling on the routes list projected through `projectTrack` and the `cos(midLat)` correction of § 51, so the same run drew two different shapes depending on which card you looked at. Both audit figures verify by computation: a metrically square loop renders **1.6064×** too wide at 51.5 °N and **exactly 2×** at 60 °N. The fix is reuse, not a corrected copy — the painter now calls `projectTrack(track, size.width, size.height, pad: 4)`, `projectTrack` loses its `@visibleForTesting` because it has a second production consumer, and the two painters now also agree on the degenerate all-one-point track (a dot, which is what the sibling already drew). **(4) The amber overlays.** § 489 reported these and left them; § 489's figures hold exactly — `#F59E0B` computes to **1.8714:1** against the light land sample and **1.9625:1** against a paler one, which is the whole 1.87–1.96 range the audit quoted, and both are under WCAG 1.4.11's 3:1 floor for a non-text element that carries meaning. `mapAccentColour` gives the selected-segment highlight, the coarse last-seen ring and the chart-hover dot the same resolved-basemap treatment the casing has: `#F59E0B` stays on the dark basemap (8.00:1) and the light one takes `#B45309`, the first darker amber rung that clears the floor, at **4.38:1** on land and still **3.13:1** over a light basemap's water fill — land is the pale end of a light basemap, and an overlay that only clears the pale fill is not legible where a riverside route runs. Hoisting the six literals to one constant and expressing the two halos as alphas of it **shrinks** § 480's data-palette entry for the file from `{F59E0B: 6}` to `{F59E0B: 1}`, the direction that guard only permits. The new darker rung is deliberately *not* added to the banned-hex list: that list is the status-role palette, and a cartographic accent is not a status role — it is pinned instead by the contrast property it exists to satisfy, which is the claim that can actually go stale.
## 492. Nothing renders as an empty hole: avatars fall back to the initial, lightboxes have a face while loading and after failing, and list surfaces hold their layout with a skeleton

**Date:** 2026-08-04

Round 7 of the issue #666 audit took the three findings whose shared root is that the app had no answer for what stands on screen while content loads or if it never arrives. **S10 (avatars):** the app carried six hand-rolled avatar implementations, and the audit's diagnosis of four of them is exactly right — `feed_screen`, `profile_screen`, `run_social_section` and `segments_panel` each painted the picture through a `DecorationImage`, which has no error hook of any kind, while gating the initial-letter child on `url == null || url.isEmpty`; a *failed* load therefore suppressed the very fallback that existed and rendered a solid primary circle with nothing in it. `settings_account_screen` had the same defect in a different costume — `CircleAvatar.backgroundImage` paints *over* its child, and the child was gated on the same condition — so five of the six were broken, not four; the sixth, `people_screen`, used `foregroundImage`, which leaves the child painted underneath and so already degraded correctly, by accident of which parameter its author reached for. All six now route through ui_kit's `IdentityAvatar` (§481), extended to take an `imageUrl` that is layered *over* the hue-derived initial rather than replacing it, with an `errorBuilder` and a `frameBuilder` that both collapse to `SizedBox.shrink()` — so the letter is what shows while the bytes are in flight and what remains if they never arrive, and the fallback can no longer be defeated by a condition. §481's byte-frozen seed→hue hash and its 360-hue AA sweep were not touched and still pass. The three `ResizeImage` decode budgets the old widgets hard-coded (96/96 for a 32 dp circle, 72/72 for 24 dp, `size * 3` for the variable one) were all the same rule written three times and became one `(size * 3).round()` inside the shared widget. This closes the avatar half of **V8**. A three-part source guard in `architecture_guards_test.dart` now fails the build on any `DecorationImage(`, any `backgroundImage:`, and any bare `NetworkImage(` in `lib/` — all three are zero today — because the trap is not a bug in one file but a shape that reads as correct at every site that repeats it.

**S9 (lightboxes):** the four photo lightboxes were near-copies differing only in row type and, for `event_photos`, the absence of a caption — verified before extracting, per the finding's own instruction. They are now one `widgets/photo_lightbox.dart` (`showPhotoLightbox(context, url:, caption:)`), and the two states it never had are the point of the extraction: a white spinner driven by `frameBuilder` (not `loadingBuilder` — `loadingBuilder` only fires once a chunk event arrives, so an image that produces no progress events shows nothing at all until the first frame, which is precisely the case the finding describes), and a broken-image icon plus two lines of localised copy on error. The error copy names the dismiss gesture explicitly, because the barrier is the only affordance and an error screen that looks like the loading screen teaches nobody how to leave. An expired signed URL is the realistic failure here — both photo widgets re-sign on a 15-minute TTL with a 5-minute refresh-ahead window, and a URL minted just before a run flips private stays valid at the Storage layer for its full TTL — so this path is reached in normal use, not only offline. Correction to the audit's counts: the app-wide "15 `Image.network`" figure counts doc-comment mentions; there were 7 real instantiations, of which 6 already had an `errorBuilder`. All 7 do now.

**S4 (skeletons):** the audit's counts verify as 102 `CircularProgressIndicator` across 67 files (not 100/65) and exactly **30** literal `Center(child: CircularProgressIndicator())` across 25 screens, with `ActivityLoader` at 4 sites. Two named things now exist where screens previously had nothing to reach for: ui_kit's `ListSkeleton(rows:)` — placeholder rows that stand where the list's rows will stand, so arriving content fills rather than re-lays-out, animated on a 900 ms pulse that holds a static pose under `disableAnimations` — and `FullBodyLoader`, the thin standard composition of `ActivityLoader` at size 76. Both take a `label` rather than defaulting to one: ui_kit has no localisations, and `ActivityLoader`'s existing `label ?? 'Loading'` was already shipping hard-coded English to every screen reader, so a new `commonLoading` key in all seven ARBs backs every call site and the four pre-existing `ActivityLoader` mounts were converted too. **This finding is deliberately half-swept, and here is the line.** Converted to `ListSkeleton` (10): `clubs_screen`, `plans_screen`, `sessions_screen`, `races_screen`, `gear_rotations_screen`, `coaching_screen`, `devices_screen`, `plan_library_screen`, `feed_screen` (3 rows at 168 dp — feed cards, not tiles), and `profile_screen`'s `_tabScope`, which covers all five profile tabs at once. Converted to `FullBodyLoader` (6 spinners + the 4 existing `ActivityLoader` mounts): `club_detail_screen`, `event_detail_screen`, `plan_detail_screen`, `workout_detail_screen`, `coach_screen`'s consent-probe frame, and `checkpoint_checkin_screen`. **Still a bare `Center(child: CircularProgressIndicator())` and owed to a later round (14):** `challenge_detail_screen:184`, `club_detail_screen:1393` and `:1510` (two in-page sections), `coach_screen:972`, `coaching_athlete_screen:142`, `live_spectator_screen:393`, `profile_screen:612` (the whole-profile load — header plus tabs, so neither a list nor a plain body), `public_route_screen:222`, `session_detail_screen:227`, `settings_body_metrics_screen:251`, `settings_safety_screen:269`, `watch_screens_editor_screen:429`, `workout_detail_screen:514`, and `run_social_section:284`. Those are section-scoped or mixed-layout loaders where the right treatment is a per-surface judgement, not a mechanical swap, which is why they were left rather than converted badly. `track_preview.dart`'s `Image.network` — the only `loadingBuilder` in the app — was left untouched: it belongs to the map/track layer another slice of this round owns.
## 493. Web gains the unsaved-changes guard and gym-session resume it was owed as the canonical surface

**Date:** 2026-08-05

Rounds 1 and 3 of the issue #666 audit shipped two capabilities on mobile and recorded that web still lacked them — a §24 inversion, since web is the canonical feature surface and mobile the additive one. Round 7 closes both. **Unsaved changes:** `trackDirty` snapshots a form's committed value and compares on demand, and `UnsavedChangesGuard.svelte` arms SvelteKit's `beforeNavigate` over it. Both of the browser's two departure paths are handled through that single hook rather than by adding a separate `beforeunload` listener: an in-app navigation is cancelled and re-driven through a shared confirm, while a `leave` navigation *is* the browser's `beforeunload` — SvelteKit turns the same `cancel()` into `preventDefault()` + `returnValue`, the browser owns the dialog text, and there is consequently no custom copy to show and nothing to render. Cancelling only while dirty is load-bearing rather than incidental: a permanently-armed `beforeunload` costs the page the engagement penalty browsers apply to one. Like mobile's §478 guard, dirtiness is probed **at navigation time** rather than tracked reactively, for the same reason — a value read at build time goes stale — but the mobile shape was deliberately not ported mechanically, because a `PopScope` predicate and a cancellable navigation event are different primitives with different capabilities. **Gym-session resume:** web's runner previously lost all state to a refresh. It now writes the same `gym_session_draft` metadata key §483 defined, with the identical field shape, and offers the same resume card on `/gym`; `restoreSessionDraft` rebuilds the runner by replaying the ordered outcome list against the current routine, so an edited routine degrades to replay-what-fits exactly as it does on mobile. Sharing the key rather than minting a web-specific one is the whole point: a session interrupted on either platform resumes on the other, which promotes the draft's field shape from a mobile implementation detail to a cross-platform contract — `metadata.md`'s entry, which had said "web and the watches ignore it", now records web as both a writer and a reader.
## 494. A tapped push routes through a pure URL→target mapper and a parked notifier, and a still-running broadcast says so

**Date:** 2026-08-05

Round 8 of the issue #666 audit closed the remainder of **I5**.
