The native-push bridge shipped with an `onOpenNotification` seam, a test for it, and `main.dart` constructing the bridge without ever supplying it — so every push tap opened the app wherever it already was and silently discarded the deep link the worker had stamped. Routing now goes `pushTargetFromUrl` → a `PushTarget` parked in a notifier → `HomeScreen` drains it. Each link in that chain is load-bearing. The mapper is **pure and total**: any base host, a relative path, a trailing slash, query or fragment junk, an unknown path and null all resolve rather than throw, with anything unrecognised degrading to the notifications inbox exactly as `pathForKind`'s own `default:` arm does. The **notifier rather than direct navigation** exists because a tap that cold-starts a terminated app is delivered before any Navigator exists; the target parks and drains on `HomeScreen`'s first frame, the same shape `incomingRouteImport` already uses for a GPX opened from a closed app. Reading **`getInitialMessage()` at attach** is equally load-bearing and was the audit's one correct suspicion: `onMessageOpenedApp` never replays the launch message, so a fix wired only to the stream works warm and fails silently cold — the precise half-fix this replaces. Corrections to the audit text: the target set is **nine** paths, not eight (the bare `/clubs` fallback `eventPath` and `clubPath` return for a row with no id was omitted), and `attach()`'s `Supabase.instance.client.auth` call sat *outside* the bridge's try/catch and throws outright when Supabase is uninitialised, contradicting the class's own L4 doc comment — now guarded, which is also what makes `attach()` testable against an available fake. Club and event targets carry a UUID against slug-addressed screens, so `SocialService` resolves the slug and degrades to the clubs hub on a miss; `/messages` has no mobile surface and lands on the inbox.

The same round found why `live_spectator_screen.dart` was an orphan, and it was not a missing menu item. The recorder pre-creates a zero-duration `runs` row so live spectator pings have a parent, and **every** public surface — web `/share/run/[id]` and mobile `PublicRunScreen` alike — rendered that stub as a finished run of 0.00 km in 0:00. Both now share `isLiveBroadcast` (`runs/live_broadcast.ts` ↔ `live_broadcast.dart`): `concluded_at` is consulted first because it is the positive terminal marker, then a zero `duration_s`, and an **absent** duration fails closed — "live" is a claim about right now and must never be inferred from a missing column. The resulting "Watch live" CTA is the tracker's first in-app entry, and it is deliberately not an invented nav destination: it sits on the surface a spectator already lands on from the feed, which was itself lying about the run. **V10's remainder** closed alongside it — `WorkoutExecutionBand` anchored on the status-bar inset while §485's column anchors at 56, so the two overlapped whenever a run started from a planned workout. `RunTopOverlay` now owns one anchor and all three slots, at `max(56, padding.top)` so folding the band in does not regress a tall cutout. Correction: §485's test could not simply be "extended" to cover this, because it pumps `RunTopBanners` standalone and never sees the band; the composed widget had to be extracted to make the invariant testable at all.
## 495. Data palettes are per-brightness and separated by luminance, and a normalised plot owes a scale

**Date:** 2026-08-05

Round 8 closed the remaining measurable contrast failures. Every figure below was computed against the real tokens, and the audit was wrong in both directions. **Medal pills:** silver drew white on `#94A3B8` at **2.56:1**; bronze, reported as failing beside it, was already **5.02:1** and was left alone. Web's rank-1 gold was the worst of the three at **2.15:1** and had never been reported at all, so gold moved onto a `--color-crown` / `--color-on-crown` pair mirroring mobile's `AppSemanticColors` (5.64 / 10.53:1), which also lifted the segment-crown icon from 1.85:1 to 6.24:1. Silver keeps its metal fill and takes dark ink (6.87 / 6.16:1) — the pill is opaque, so its foreground is free to change and its fill carries the meaning. **S6 (training load):** one fixed trio cannot clear 3:1 in both themes — indigo is 2.57:1 on the dark card (the audit's ~2.6 was right) and amber **1.94:1** on the light card (which the audit missed entirely) — so each brightness carries its own triple. Pairwise 3:1 *between* three series is unreachable once each also owes 3:1 to its card (light's whole usable range is 5.98:1), so what the guard pins between them is a monotone luminance ladder, not a pairwise floor. The same finding's second half was real: the plot was min/max-normalised with no gutter, so CTL 45 and CTL 450 drew identically; both platforms gained round ticks and gridlines, with web's labels in a CSS gutter *beside* the SVG because `preserveAspectRatio="none"` squashes any text inside the viewBox. **S8 (HR zones):** three surfaces carried three different five-colour lists while `intensity_card`'s own comment claimed it matched web `--zone-*` vars that **did not exist** and a run-detail band it **did not match**. Measured, the unaudited run-detail band was the worse of the two: adjacent bands at 1.32:1, the whole ramp spanning 2.11:1, four of five under 3:1. Five pairwise-3:1 bands are arithmetically impossible — four steps of 3:1 needs 81:1 and sRGB offers 21:1 — so the contract is inverted: every band clears 3:1 against its *surface*, and the separators between segments are drawn in that surface colour, which makes each boundary guaranteed visible against both neighbours. **Map attribution:** round 7 left the type size open; §482's 11 px floor applies, and the credit — a link with a neighbour 6 dp away, so WCAG 2.5.8's spacing exception cannot be claimed — also owes a 24×24 dp target. It keeps a bespoke `TextStyle` rather than `labelSmall` because the strip is mounted inside the rasterised share cards: the size follows the theme's floor as a constant, the colour still follows the resolved basemap per §491. Finally, **semantic bases are foregrounds too**: the readiness delta used raw literals (3.15 / 3.25:1 on the dark card) on mobile and bare base tokens (3.28 / 4.14:1) on web, each failing AA in the theme the other passed, so `app_semantic_colors_test` now holds every base to 4.5:1 **as text** on card and scaffold rather than only 3:1 as a banner fill. The §480 literal allowlist shrank by six occurrences and gained no entries.
## 496. The worker emits stable ids and web resolves them, and a surface showing someone else's row links to the public twin

**Date:** 2026-08-05

Round 8 traced a live defect out of the push work: `pathForKind` — the single kind→URL map behind the email CTA, the web-push payload and the native-push message — emitted `/events/{id}` and `/notifications`, and **neither is a route**. Enumerating all fifteen kinds against the real route tree found three more the hand-off had missed. `run_completed` → `/runs/{id}` was dead because the trigger inserts one row **per follower**, so the recipient is never the run's owner and the owner-scoped page renders "Run not found" — every "a runner you follow finished a run" email dead-ended. `club_post` → `/clubs/{club_id}` matched `/clubs/[slug]` structurally while resolving by slug, so a UUID matched nothing. And `content_hidden`, added by a later migration, fell through `default:` to the dead inbox path. The root cause is that web already had a canonical routing table, `social/notification_link.ts`, that the worker had silently diverged from. `NotificationRow` genuinely cannot carry the club slug an event URL needs — the projections select one row's own FK columns and `pathForKind` is pure and shared by three render functions — so the rule is now explicit: **the worker emits stable-id URLs and web owns id→canonical resolution.** That is not merely the cheaper option; a slug baked into an email breaks on the next club rename, whereas the id URL is permanent. Both halves shipped, because a fix that only changes what *future* links say leaves every link already sitting in an inbox broken forever — `/events/[id]` and the `/clubs/[slug]` id fallback are therefore load-bearing permanently. The durable part is the guard: `notification_link_guard_test.go` parses the `NotificationKind` union from `types.ts`, walks `apps/web/src/routes` building a matcher per route, and asserts every kind × every FK-presence permutation resolves — proven to fire by reverting the fix. The Go tests had pinned the broken strings, which is exactly how this survived: **a guard on an outbound link must assert that the target resolves, not that the emitter produced a particular string.** The same mistake had been made independently on web, where the social feed linked another runner's entry to `/runs/{id}` and the page presented a public run as deleted — silently, and looking correct to the run's owner. Other-people surfaces link to `/share/run/[id]` and its siblings; only own-data surfaces use the owner routes. One more rung was missing under that lesson: **resolving is not arriving.** The `/clubs/{id}` half forwards inside its own route, and a same-route param change is the one navigation SvelteKit serves by reusing the component rather than remounting it — so `onMount`, the only caller of the club page's fetch, never fired again and every id link landed on the correct canonical URL and then sat on "Loading club…" for good. The Go guard was green throughout, correctly: it proves a path matches a route, which is a weaker claim than the page rendering the thing the link named. The forward therefore re-enters `load()` itself after the `goto`, passing the resolved slug down as an argument rather than re-reading the reactive `slug` — after `goto` resolves the derived has not necessarily propagated, so a pass that re-read it could see the uuid again and forward again. Bounded twice over: only a uuid forwards (`isEntityId` at the call site, and `fetchClubSlugById` returns null for anything else), and a canonical slug is never a uuid. `tests-e2e/clubs/id-deep-links.spec.ts` asserts the resolved page's **title** rather than its URL, which is what makes an empty arrival fail.
## 497. Text inside a fixed box is bounded three ways, by what the box is for

**Date:** 2026-08-05

Round 8 closed **V12**. The audit named 23 sites; a depth-0 scan finds **17**, of which **14 were real** — the gap is brace-matching that counts a spacer `SizedBox` nested anywhere inside a card that also holds a `Text`. Two more genuine sites existed that no literal scan can see, so 16 were fixed in total. The fixes divide by what the box *is*. A **layout** box in a scrollable column grows (`ConstrainedBox(minHeight:)`, or `IntrinsicHeight` with `CrossAxisAlignment.stretch` where a strip must stay uniform). A **chart label lane** is a text-derived dimension and scales through `MediaQuery.textScalerOf(context)`, preserving the 1.0x geometry exactly. Text inside a **fixed-diameter graphic** whose size is load-bearing — a progress ring, a macro ring, a calendar day dot, an avatar, the run screen's Start circle — takes `BoxFit.scaleDown`, so 1.0x is untouched and a larger setting is fitted to what the graphic can hold, which is strictly more legible than the crop it replaces. Two findings matter beyond the mechanism. The this-week strip's fill bar rode an `Expanded` lane that the doubled labels squeezed to **exactly zero**, so the chart rendered blank for precisely the users who set large text — a fixed height can delete data, not merely clip it. And the Start circle was **already broken at 1.0x**: English "START" fills 117.5 of the 124 px interior, so French "DÉMARRER" was breaking mid-glyph before text scaling entered the picture — locale is a text-scale axis. Corrections to the audit text: `segments_panel.dart:824` does not exist (the nearest height wraps a spinner that is the other branch of a ternary from the text), and `event_detail_screen`'s "18 around a `fontSize: 10`" is not a box height at all but ui_kit's `IdentityAvatar`, a real clip fixed at the root for every avatar in the app. Deliberately unchanged and recorded so a later sweep does not "finish" them: `home_screen`'s 64 px nav items (58 px of content at 2x), the run screen's 56 px lap badge (45×32 inside 56, consistent with §486), photo tiles that bound images rather than text, and the fixed-canvas share rasterisers. The next sweep should match **computed** heights, not only literals: `nutrition_screen`'s week chart reads `barArea + 24` and overflowed 12 px per column.
## 498. A destructive mobile confirm is built by `confirmDestructive`, and a swipe is not an affordance

**Date:** 2026-08-05

Round 8 closed **U7** and **C11**, and the audit had the second one backwards. Counted on `main`: 88 `AlertDialog`s, of which 26 use two `TextButton`s — and **21 of those already carried destructive emphasis**, leaving only 3 unmarked, not the ~20 the audit claimed. Rounds 4–7 had effectively finished that family one dialog at a time; the unmarked-destructive problem had migrated to the `FilledButton` side, where 11 of 58 carried emphasis. (Counting this correctly requires stripping *nested* `AlertDialog` blocks first, or a parent inherits credit for its child's emphasis.) `lib/widgets/confirm_destructive.dart` now owns the shape — cancel first and unstyled, confirm second in the error colour, barrier dismiss resolving `false` — and `confirmDiscard` delegates to it, so one `AlertDialog` construction serves the whole family. The confirm **label is required** and must name the consequence rather than agree with the question: colour is a second signal a colour-blind reader may not receive, so the verb has to carry the meaning alone. **Destructive** means it destroys data, or a relationship the user cannot restore on their own — delete, remove, clear, erase, discard, revoke, unlink, deny, leave. It does not mean merely consequential: reconnecting an integration, un-archiving a conversation, replacing an active plan and an upsert-only restore are all recoverable by the same user from the same surface, and prompting alike on both teaches the user to dismiss without reading. The tempting "one-way ⇒ destructive" test was rejected — abandoning a plan is one-way and destroys nothing. A source guard in `architecture_guards_test.dart` classifies every dialog and fails an unemphasised destructive confirm outside a reviewed exempt set, so the classification is made deliberately rather than by omission.

The U7 sweep found a live bug inside itself. The coach archive drawer carried the app's only list-row `Dismissible`, and its `confirmDismiss` read `(_) => _deleteArchive(t)` — which *performs* the delete and returns whether it succeeded. A stray swipe erased an archived conversation with **no prompt and no undo**, while the row's subtitle advertised the gesture in seven languages. Destructive row actions now use the `PopupMenuButton` idiom the rest of the app already uses, behind `confirmDestructive`, and a guard fails any new `Dismissible` outside `top_banner.dart`, where dismissal destroys nothing. An inline icon button that is the *only* affordance on its row stays — it is visible and labelled, and the rule is against hidden destruction, not inline destruction; all 29 `Icons.delete` sites were classified and none mixes idioms. Long-press multi-select stays on runs and routes, where bulk delete is real, as a secondary accelerator over a visible per-row path — though it still has no discoverability hint on either screen, which is owed to a later round.
## 499. `pubspec.lock` is committed, and a test may not leak a timer the library owns

**Date:** 2026-08-05

Round 8's integration run surfaced a defect none of the audits could have: **`main` was red in CI and no commit of ours had caused it.** `pubspec.lock` was gitignored, so every fresh checkout — CI included — resolved the newest versions the constraints allowed. `postgrest 2.9.1`, `supabase_flutter 2.17.1` and `realtime_client 2.13.0` were published at 08:47 on 2026-08-05, hours after the last green run on `main`, and `realtime_client 2.13.0` arms a 50 s pending-disconnect timer from *inside* `RealtimeChannel.unsubscribe`. Screens call that from `dispose`, so the timer does not exist until the tree is torn down and no amount of pumping inside a test body can drain it: 34 widget tests across the four channel-holding screens began failing `!timersPending`. The lockfile is now committed. These are applications, not libraries, and the lockfile is the only thing that makes CI, a fresh worktree and a developer's checkout resolve the same code — its absence is also why parallel agents kept verifying against a dependency set neither CI nor each other had. Upgrades become a deliberate act with their own CI run, which is what Dependabot is already wired for. **This was diagnosed twice before it was diagnosed correctly**, which is the more useful lesson: an agent reported the failures as pre-existing, and a fresh worktree at `main` appeared to confirm it — the control that settled it was running the *same commit* in the *main checkout*, which differed only in resolved dependencies. When a test fails in one tree and passes in another at the same SHA, the difference is the environment, and an unpinned dependency graph is the first place to look.

Pinning alone would have been a crutch, so the tests were fixed too. `test/realtime_drain.dart` wraps `testWidgets` with an unmount-and-pump-past-the-timer teardown, and the nine test files that mount a channel-holding screen use it. The full mobile suite now passes on **both** resolutions — 2.11.0 and 2.13.0 — so the pin holds a proven-green baseline rather than hiding an incompatibility, and the eventual Dependabot bump is pre-verified. The rule this leaves: a widget test must not leak a timer, including one a library arms on teardown where the app has no handle to cancel it; the drain belongs in shared test support, not copy-pasted per file, because the next library to do this will hit the same nine files.
## 500. The horizontal axis adds a fourth mechanism — the row reflows — and every width in this issue was measured in the wrong font

**Date:** 2026-08-05

Round 9 closed the horizontal half of §497. The vertical three transpose directly (a box grows via `minWidth`; a lane is text-derived through `MediaQuery.textScalerOf`; text inside a graphic whose size is load-bearing takes `BoxFit.scaleDown`), and width needs a fourth that height did not: **the row reflows**. A `Row` of text becomes a `Wrap`, and `WrapAlignment.spaceAround`/`spaceBetween` lay a single run out exactly as the `Row` did — so 1.0x is byte-identical and the reflow only fires when the content genuinely does not fit. It is preferred to ellipsis wherever a truncated label stops being a name: "Carboh…" is not a macro. The four sites divide cleanly — run-detail's split lanes are an *aligned column*, so they scale (a per-row intrinsic width would go ragged and misalign the bars), while the ring strip, the map credit strip and the mileage toggle are *runs of independent items*, so they wrap.

**The measurement finding outlasts the mechanism, and invalidates figures throughout this issue.** `flutter_test`'s default font is fixed-advance — every glyph exactly one em — so every absolute width quoted by the original audit *and by §497* is 2–6× too large. Measured against real Roboto via `FontLoader` across all seven ARB locales at 320/360/411 dp, the map credit strip is 31–84 px over at 411 dp rather than 181, and the nutrition ring strip is clean in English at 1.5x rather than 55 px over. The standing rule that follows: **a committed guard may not assert an absolute fit**, because CI cannot render the device's font. Pin the derivation — that a lane grew by the same factor as the text it holds, that a label stayed inside its container — which is font-independent and holds *a fortiori* under the wider test font. Measure absolutes against a real proportional font before quoting them anywhere.

**`SegmentedButton` is retired from any container narrower than its intrinsic width, and §486's exemption is amended.** That exemption treated it as a framework-managed internal with no knob to bind, which is right for narrow width; the same fact makes it fail text scaling in *both* directions. Given room it pushed its labels 88 px past a 411 dp card; given a bounded parent it squeezed its segments and clipped the labels *inside* them with no ellipsis and no exception — French "Semaine" got 66.7 px of the 109.9 it needed at 320 dp / 2x. Reflowing the container alone would have hidden the burst and kept the clip, so the control was replaced with chips in a `Wrap`, which also restores the M3 checkmark it had suppressed for width, so selection is no longer colour-only. Corrections to the audit: the depth-0 scan finds **505** numeric `width:` arguments, of which **34** enclose text and only **19** are real text lanes. Deliberately unchanged: `home_screen:739`'s nav caption, which ellipsizes cleanly and is §497's recorded exemption; the mileage card's spotlight-headline `Row`, a short stat beside an `Expanded` sibling that §486 swept and left; and the 13 remaining `SegmentedButton` sites, which carry the same exposure and are owed a measured sweep of their own.
## 501. An aligned text lane is `TextLane`, and a fixed box around text fails two ways, only one of which looks like a bug

**Date:** 2026-08-05

Round 9 closed 16 lanes across 11 files, measured against real Roboto per §500. **Six were live at 1.0x**, not the three the survey named: French "Semaine de fin de programme" needs 186.4 px of a 70 px box, Portuguese "Desaquecimento" 105.7 of 90, "28 de mar." 66.1 of 56 — and beside it "10:35 AM" needs 57.9, a two-digit hour clearing a box a one-digit hour fits, which is why the survey read the time as a 1.5x problem. Both rank lanes lose at 1.0x on a four-digit rank the survey never sampled.

**The audit's word for the failure was wrong throughout, and that is why fifteen of these shipped.** None of these `Text`s sets `maxLines`, so nothing clips. A label with a break opportunity **reflows inside its box** and makes its row taller than the column around it; one without **paints straight over the lane beside it**, because a `SizedBox` does not clip. The first is invisible as a bug and the second reads as a rendering glitch — neither reads as "text too wide for its box", which is what everyone was looking for. Twelve sites take `TextLane` (ui_kit): the literal read as a *floor* through `MediaQuery.textScalerOf`, collapsing §497's mechanisms 1 and 2 into one widget, so 1.0x is pixel-identical, the lane tracks the scale, and content that still outruns it widens the lane rather than losing characters. Three needed a different shape, and the difference is the durable lesson. The plan-preview phase is a localized *phrase*, and no floor rescues a 186 px phrase in a 70 px row, so it takes §486's treatment — `Expanded` + ellipsis on the label, flex removed from the two numerics so **a value can never be the thing that truncates**. The workout-structure row is a term beside its value, where a lane is actively dangerous: a `Row` sizes non-flexible children before giving what remains to `Expanded`, so an unbounded floor can starve the value to zero — §497's "a fixed height can delete data" recurring on the other axis. That pair reflows instead. A narrow source guard keeps the class closed without fighting the `BoxFit.scaleDown` graphics §497 settled, and it names all 15 pre-fix boxes at the exact line numbers the audit quoted, covering a re-plan-preview lane no widget test can reach.
## 502. A stat row reflows on a text-derived column width, a toolbar has three slots, and a FAB's clearance is derived rather than picked

**Date:** 2026-08-05

Round 9 closed C2, C4 and C5, and the audit's numbers were low on all three. Run detail's secondary row was one `Row` of up to eight `Expanded` cells: **40.0 dp each** on a 360 dp phone, under every value it draws — and because `_StatSmall` ellipsises rather than overflows, **nothing threw**. No debug banner, no test, just an unreadable screen for the hilly-race-with-a-chest-strap case. `_StatGrid` derives its column count from the width a cell needs *at the current text scale*, so eight stats become two rows of four at 1.0x and four rows of two at 2.0x, and the secondary row finally shares a column grid with the primary row above it. The same grid took the heart-rate summary row, which was three unbounded `_StatSmall` in a bare `Row` and genuinely overflowed at 2.0x — a §486 site the round-5 sweep missed because its texts sit two widgets down.

Route detail's toolbar carried six concurrent owner actions. A Material toolbar spends 72 dp before the title and 48 per action, so the title gets `width − 88 − 48n`, and six leaves **0 dp — not a crushed name, no name at all**; the audit said 24, having assumed 48 for the leading slot Flutter gives 56. `run_detail_screen` had solved this by hand for four actions and left a comment saying so, so `AppBarActions` is that answer as one widget, and `sim_watch_screen` — a third instance nobody had counted — takes it too. A `destructive` action is never promoted into a visible slot: a toolbar icon carries no label, and §498's reasoning about naming the consequence applies before the dialog as well as inside it.

The FAB finding was the one where every existing number was a guess: four screens reserved nothing, six reserved four different values, and the largest still under-cleared a stacked pair by 60 dp. `fabScrollClearance` reads `MediaQuery.padding` rather than `viewPadding`, which is what makes it composable — a `SafeArea` above the caller, or a parent `Scaffold` with a `bottomNavigationBar`, has already consumed the nav bar and reports zero, and adding it again would leave a dead band. **Two audit claims did not survive measurement** and are recorded so a later round does not "fix" them: route detail's fixed 88 was *adequate*, because its list sits inside a `SafeArea` and Flutter 3.41 zeroes `viewPadding` for its descendants — **§C20's diagnosis is stale for this Flutter version**; and `plans_screen`'s comment that "Scaffold does NOT automatically pad FABs" is likewise stale, its compensating `Padding` having floated the button ~48 dp too high on 3-button navigation ever since `endFloat` learned `minViewPadding`. The general lesson is the one the 0 dp title makes concrete: a layout constant that was true of some Flutter version decays silently, so the durable form is a helper that derives the number and a guard that fails the next screen which hard-codes one.
## 503. A status token is a foreground or a fill, never both, and a chip tint is measured where it lands

**Date:** 2026-08-05

Round 9 finished the web half of §495. **96** sites across 46 files still set `color: var(--color-success)` / `var(--color-danger)` directly — success at **3.282:1** on the card and **2.968:1** on the page, below even the 3:1 non-text floor — and all moved onto the `-text` pair. Measuring the swap honestly exposed two things a plain-surface figure hides, one of them a defect in §495's own work. **The dark `-text` tokens were aliased to the base hue**, which reads 5.286:1 on the card but **4.059:1 on the same-hue chip tint** most of those sites actually paint: the token comment's claimed parity with mobile's `AppSemanticColors` was true in light and false in dark. Both now carry mobile's real pair, and the lockstep is asserted rather than described. And three RSVP pills stacked a tint over an already-tinted parent — 18% over 14% composites to 29.5%, giving **3.345:1** — so a status tint carrying same-status text is now mixed against an opaque surface, which cannot compound.

The ban is on **foreground** use across `color` / `fill` / `stroke` / `-webkit-text-fill-color`; fills, tints, borders and the white-on-`-strong` pairing are what these tokens are for. That distinction rests on a single lookbehind character, so an 18-case fixture table pins the matcher in both directions — six must-flag, twelve must-spare — and the guard was proved to fire six ways, including by deleting the boundary and watching the fixtures catch it. Two further data palettes S8 never reached were folded onto the shared ladder: the intensity split bar, whose amber is 2.148:1 on the light card but whose real defect is **1.032:1 against its own partner in dark** — `--color-primary` flips to coral and coral *is* the amber, so the split bar showed no split at all — and the dashboard's per-zone bars, the fifth HR-zone list in the codebase and the worst measured yet, with z3 and z4 **1.016:1** apart in light and z1–z4 inside **1.08:1** in dark. Two bands can be pairwise 3:1 where five cannot, so easy/hard take `--zone-1`/`--zone-5` rather than a third bespoke pair. The zone-name tints were deleted rather than recoloured: `--zone-5` is 3.592:1 and cannot be text, and a label tinted a hue its own bar does not draw is §489's mislabelled-key defect one level up. **Left open with numbers:** `css_token_guard.test.ts` only fails on *fallback-less* `var(--x)`, so **129 fallback-hidden references to tokens that do not exist** survive across ~41 files — `var(--chip-fg, #335)` at **1.344:1** on the dark card, `var(--color-error, #b71c1c)` at 2.460:1, `var(--text-muted, #6b7280)` at 3.344:1. Those declarations never track the theme at all; it is the same bug class that guard's own doc comment describes, wearing a fallback.
